items.label: Virgin cotton fibre, upper quartile length

components.text: In the same trial, a 30s ring-spun yarn took at most **25%** recycled cotton. So this collection is remade as fabric, with the fibre left whole

footnote: Source: Arafat & Uddin, Heliyon (2022), industrial-scale spinning-mill trial. A third shorter is calculated: (28.3 − 18.9) ÷ 28.3. The lines are drawn to scale
notes: Why I only unpick and never shred. Mechanical recycling chops cotton fibres short. In an industrial-scale trial at a spinning mill, virgin cotton had an upper quartile length of 28.3 millimetres and post-consumer recycled cotton only 18.9, about a third shorter by my own calculation from those two figures. Short fibre has to be blended with new cotton, and in a 30s ring-spun yarn recycled cotton could make up at most 25%. Unpick a whole piece and sew it again, and its colour, its wear and its original fibre are all still there. That is why this project stays at the level of fabric.
